His Outlines of Pyrrhonism set out the scepticism inherited from Pyrrho: every argument meets an argument of equal force, so the sceptic suspends judgement, epoché, and gains tranquillity of mind, ataraxia. En 1932, Frederic Bartlett, titulaire de: In 1932, Frederic Bartlett, who had held the chair of experimental psychology at Cambridge since the year before, published Remembering. In it he reports his repeated-reproduction experiments: English people read a Native American tale, The War of the Ghosts, then retold it several times, at longer and longer intervals. Much of the story was forgotten, and what did not fit their culture disappeared or became familiar: canoes became boats. Bartlett drew from it a theory of schemas: remembering is not replaying a trace, it is reconstructing, from one's experience, knowledge and expectations. He also treats memory as a social fact and describes transmission-chain studies, in which a story passes from person to person.

In it he gathers history's collective follies: three financial bubbles, Law's Mississippi scheme, the South Sea Bubble and tulip mania; but also the Crusades, the witch hunts of the 16th and 17th centuries, the alchemists, fortune-tellers, haunted houses, relics and prophecies. The 1852 edition reorganised it into two volumes; later editions took the title that stuck, Extraordinary Popular Delusions and the Madness of Crowds.
